summary: Record inactive requester cancellation and withdrawal intent under adopted Agent Policy v3; never signal or stop processes.

replay.detail: Uses existing job.recorded transitions. Pre-unit-6 records without reason remain valid and replicate/fold unchanged. Queued cancellation becomes withdrawn; running cancellation becomes cancel-requested only. Deterministic same-head cancellation races append one transition and refuse the stale snapshot with job-state-changed.

schema.detail: POST /v1/client/jobs/{job/id}/cancel uses the existing slash-bearing ID catch-all, dispatching only the /cancel suffix. Add optional string reason to the job.recorded claim schema, preserving typed intent reasons beside the transition record. This changes the registry digest, not the SQLite schema.

rules.detail: Only authenticated session.actor matching the recorded requester may call cancel. Bound-identity fences inherited from unit 5 apply to all jobs methods. Missing identity refuses; no caller JSON, environment marker or operator override supplies authority. Internal DaemonLimit provenance permits max-hold/deadline or mission-budget stop intent, but has no API route.

compatibility.detail: Older jobs readers retain claims carrying reason as waiting unknown-field records until upgrade; pre-jobs readers retain job.recorded as unknown-kind records. Exchanges and known-claim projection continue. Upgraded readers accept old records without reason; restart retries the original immutable waiting claims and canonical replay projects them. Adopted policy: disconnected waits never cancel or permit reruns. Explicit requester-lease expiry withdraws queued jobs with requester-lease-expired; running jobs keep running and retain declared max-hold/deadline enforcement. Their outcome remains retrievable under the same requester/key. Withdrawn jobs retain their receipt: same key returns withdrawn, a new attempt requires a new key. No job-requester lease exists in the current jobs model, so expiry is a trusted explicit pure-decision input, not a session/actor/step-lease timer.

downtime.detail: Disabled by the existing explicit jobs configuration gate; admission and runtime enforcement remain not wired. No limit, timeout or concurrency defaults are added.

manual.detail: HTTP 403 not-requester/requester-unresolved; 409 job-terminal/job-state-uncertain/job-state-changed; existing jobs-disabled and stale errors unchanged. operator-stop is reserved for a later audited person-scoped unit 9 stop inside the daemon, never agent kill commands.

recovery.detail: Repeated cancel is idempotent. Unit 9 alone confirms whole-tree stop before cancelled. Running orphans remain subject to declared max-hold/deadline through DaemonLimit with max-hold; no forever-capacity or implicit-rerun policy is introduced.
